label: the crawler (models/headcrab.mdl): a sludge crawler: low, wet, six-legged, the size of a headcrab, grey-green with a pale belly and a ring of teeth

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/chumtoad.mdl, models/roach.mdl, models/leech.mdl: the judge does not know which
measured.contract: keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: Low and headcrab-sized (25.9 x 28.3 x 13.5), and the six-legged outline is there, but some of it doesn't read as the brief describes. The front pair of legs sticks straight forward on each side of the mouth like tusks (LEFT, RIGHT and TOP views), so from the side and top only four legs read as legs. The body is a smooth capsule with a flat round cap at the rear (BACK, BACK-LEFT, BACK-RIGHT). Two blunt cylinder stumps stick up from the rear of the back (FRONT, BACK, LEFT), and nothing in the brief accounts for them.

M2.reason: The brief gives no size beyond 'the size of a headcrab'. 25.9 long, 28.3 wide and 13.5 high is headcrab scale and low, as asked.

M3.reason: A pale belly (BELOW) and a ring of teeth in a red mouth (FRONT) are there. Six legs are modelled (BELOW shows three per side), but the front pair is horizontal, doesn't reach the floor and reads as mandibles (LEFT, RIGHT), so it stands on four. Every leg is a single unjointed cone. The two stumps on the back are extra parts the brief doesn't ask for.

M4.reason: The colours match the brief: grey-green body, pale cream belly, dark red mouth with white teeth. The 'wet' sludge material isn't there. The surface is matte and flat-lit, with no sheen, gloss or slime anywhere, and reads as dry clay or painted plastic (TOP, FRONT-LEFT).

M5.reason: There is some detail: dark spots, pale scratch streaks and small bumps on the back (TOP). It is sparse, soft and low-contrast next to Half-Life's creature skins, with no slime, drips, veining or texture on the legs or belly. The belly in BELOW is one flat faceted cream colour.

M6.reason: Ours is plainly C in the line-up. Next to D (the chumtoad, with its mottled purple skin, glowing eye and spiky jointed legs), C looks like a smooth, sparsely textured bean on peg legs. A player would see a placeholder-grade creature rather than one of the game's own.

M7.reason: The mouth faces forward and the model is upright. In the run frames the belly sits on the floor line at the origin, as a headcrab does.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. 696 triangles is plausibly under twice the median for Half-Life creatures of this size, though the median itself isn't in the measurements. Nothing is open, inside out or floating in any view.

C1.reason: Nothing comes apart, and in the jump (JUMP 0-30) the body leaps, turns nose-up and lands whole. Through WALK 0/34 to 34/34, though, the legs hardly move: the body glides with the cones held rigid, so it doesn't crawl the way a six-legged walker should. Leg tips dip slightly below the floor line in several walk frames (e.g. WALK 5/34, 24/34).

C2.reason: Measured: it keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts, so the game's own headcrab code drives it.
